subject: BrightCart POC results: short quote + permission to publish
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightcart.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart POC results and next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for running this POC with us. Attached is a short outcomes pack (BrightCart_POC_metrics_20280624.pdf) with the metrics we promised to surface. TL;DR: across the pilot traffic (mix of cart search and recommendations) we saw a ~18% reduction in average CPU time per request and a 22% improvement in tail latency (p95) when using our serving runtime + KV prefix caching, while maintaining identical downstream relevance scores. Cost per effective inference token reduced ~14% versus your baseline batching config.

Would BrightCart be comfortable sharing a one-line endorsement we can include in a short customer snapshot? Example: “Redwood cut inference cost and latency while keeping quality intact.” If that’s too open, happy to propose wording.

If you’re okay with a quick 10–15 minute alignment call this week, Jordan and I can walk through the metrics and the one-liner. Otherwise, a reply with a one-line quote and publication permission is totally fine.

Attaching: BrightCart_POC_metrics_20280624.pdf

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

Redwood Inference — production-first inference platform

Thanks Marcus — this looks great at a glance. Appreciate the concise pack. Two quick clarifications before I sign off on a quote:

- The 18% CPU reduction — is that across the 30-day pilot or during peak-hour synthetic replay?
- Can you provide a 1–2 sentence version of the proposed quote we’d be asked to approve (so my execs have a clean thing to say)?

If it’s easier, we can do a short sync on Thursday — 10 minutes would be ideal. Otherwise send the suggested quote and I’ll push to Legal/Comms for sign-off.

Cheers,

Jordan / Monica — quick internal: Elena asked two clarifying points and wants a suggested one-liner to run up the chain. Can you help draft a tight quote we can propose? Please keep it customer-first and avoid percentages in the quote to reduce legal friction (we can keep exact metrics in the pack).

Suggested constraints: one sentence, company-level (BrightCart), one benefit-focused phrase (cost/latency/quality).

I’ve attached the metrics pdf.

Thanks — Marcus

Quick draft — please edit: 

"Redwood’s inference platform helped BrightCart reduce operational inference cost while improving response time, without impacting model quality."

If you want a shorter variant: "Redwood lowered our inference cost and improved response time while preserving model quality."

Monica — any red-team / legal flags on either phrasing?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 11:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightCart POC results and next steps

Elena — thanks for the quick reply. To answer your question: the 18% CPU reduction is the weighted average across the pilot traffic (production-like replay of the 30-day window). We’ve left the full breakdown in the attached PDF for Legal/Comms.

Below are two short options you can share with your execs — pick whichever is easiest for approvals, or edit directly: 

1) "Redwood’s inference platform helped BrightCart reduce operational inference cost while improving response time, without impacting model quality."
2) "Redwood lowered our inference cost and improved response time while preserving model quality."

If either looks good, reply to this email with the chosen line and a short permission note (e.g., "BrightCart approves use of this quote and BrightCart logo for a customer snapshot"). If you prefer a 10-minute call, I’m free Thu 9:30–10:30am PT — let me know.

Thanks again,
Marcus

--
